note: Three designated primitive camping spots, each beside a small gravel parking lot on the area's one gravel lane east off Route D: at the entrance on Route D, about 650 m in, and 100 m further at the fishing pond where the lane ends. No built pads, tables or toilets; a rig stays on a lot with old field and timber around it. No water. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC designates camping beside three small lots (GIS points at all three, map symbols at two) - stays under the lot rule, but there is no built camp: rigs on the lots. Phone matches. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Not waterfront stands. Pin 22 m from the pond lot (minor).
flags: BUILT CAMPS VERSUS LOTS: no built camp anywhere. The page lists 'Individual Campsites'; the brochure (12/2025) says only 'Camping is permitted in designated areas and is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' The 05/15 map legend has 'Primitive Camping Area' and draws the symbol twice: at the Parking Lot in the south-west corner on Route D, and at the Parking Lot about 650 m east along the gravel lane; the third lot, at the Fishing Pond where the lane ends, has no camping symbol on the map. GIS layer 27 has three 'Primitive Camping Area' points: 39.37289,-93.68188 (west lot, 30 m from it in old field), 39.37282,-93.67445 (middle lot, 30 m from it in timber) and 39.37225,-93.67376 (pond lot, 20 m from it in old field - the stored pin). Imagery (leaf-off, 0.28 m/px): the west lot is a gravel apron about 30 x 15 m at the corner of Route D and the lane; the middle and pond lots are gravel pads about 15 x 20 m each, 100 m apart, the second a turnaround at the lane's end with the small fishing pond 15 m south. Nothing else is built at any of them (no pads, rings, tables, privy). Each is designated lot-side camping (the Lick Creek case), so it stays under the 2026-11-09 rules; none is 'the campground' more than the others, and the middle and pond lots together are the natural place for the pin (off the road, by the pond).

PIN (minor): stored 39.37225,-93.67376 is the GIS point in old-field brush 22 m north-east of the pond lot. The lot is 39.37213,-93.67396. Not worth a move on its own. The fourth GIS lot (39.37951,-93.67321, on Route E) has no camping point.

ACCESS: paved Route E and Route D, then about 650 m of single-lane gravel to the middle and pond lots; no ford, no posted limit, no 4WD wording. The two inner lots are small (a 23-ft rig fits, with little room to spare if other vehicles are parked).
BROCHURE: 'Unattended camp or warming fires are prohibited. All fires may be restricted during times of extreme fire danger.' No campsite seasons; no lot is named for camping.
WATER: the fishing pond is well under 5 acres (a pond: no value). Turkey Creek is on the detached east tract. Not waterfront stands.
PHONE: stored 660-646-6122 matches the page's 'For more information call (660) 646-6122' (brochure: 'Grand Pass Conservation Area 660/595-2444 or Chillicothe Office 660/646-6122').
Nothing else in the database within 3 km. No split: the three spots share one lane and are under 750 m apart.
